title: Caring for a nephrostomy at home
what: A nephrostomy is a thin tube from the kidney through the skin of your back that drains urine into a bag. At home you look after it every day.
why: When something blocks urine from leaving the kidney - a stone, a narrowing or a tumor - and the doctor has placed a tube.
duration: care usually takes 10 to 15 minutes; the dressing is usually changed every 2 to 3 days or more often, as your doctor says
tell_doctor: If there is little urine in the bag or it stops coming
If there is blood in the urine or the urine is cloudy
If the dressing often gets wet
All your medicines, especially blood thinners

prepare.title: Training
prepare.text: Before discharge, ask the nurse to show you how to change the dressing and bag.

prepare.title: Supplies
prepare.text: Keep bags, sterile gauze, tape and antiseptic at home.

prepare.title: Bag
prepare.text: The bag must always be below the kidney - this keeps urine from flowing back.

prepare.title: Water
prepare.text: Your doctor will tell you how much to drink. Usually you are advised to drink enough.

bring: A stock of urine bags and dressings
The discharge summary and the urology contacts
Notes of how much urine you pass
steps: Wash your hands and put on gloves
Take off the old dressing without pulling the tube
Look at the skin around it for redness or discharge
Clean the skin with antiseptic as you were taught
Put on a clean dressing and tape the tube
Check that the tube is not bent
Empty the bag when it is half full
feel: Sometimes an aching feeling in your side
The tube gets in the way of sleeping on that side - you get used to it over time
after: Write down the urine amount if your doctor asked
You can usually shower with the dressing protected - no baths; ask your doctor
The tube is replaced at the hospital on a schedule
Do not lift heavy things or pull on the tube
red_flags: The tube came out - cover the spot with a clean gauze and go to the hospital right away, because the opening closes quickly
Urine stopped coming and you have severe pain in your side - see a doctor urgently
Fever or chills - see a doctor urgently, and if you feel very weak, call your local emergency number
A lot of blood or clots in the bag

faq.q: Can I sleep on my side with a nephrostomy?
faq.a: Yes, if the tube is not squeezed. It is easier to sleep on your back or on the other side.

faq.q: What if urine leaks around the tube?
faq.a: Change the dressing and tell your doctor - the tube may have moved or be blocked.

reminders.text: Nephrostomy dressing change tomorrow. Check your supply of gauze and bags.
